---
title: "Solution: Mining Rules from the Health Insurance Dataset"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(arules)
library(arulesViz)

options(bdat602.source_only = TRUE)
source("courses/bdat-602/_teacher/resources/datasets/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_data <- simulate_bdat602(n = 500000, seed = 602)
```

## Task 1: Prepare the transaction object

```{r task1-transactions}
flag_cols <- c("dental_cover", "vision_cover", "mental_cover", "maternity_cover")

trans_df <- health_data |>
  select(all_of(flag_cols)) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), as.logical))

trans <- as(trans_df, "transactions")
summary(trans)
```

## Task 2: Plot item frequencies

```{r task2-item-freq}
itemFrequencyPlot(
  trans,
  topN  = 4,
  type  = "relative",
  main  = "Relative Item Frequency — Insurance Add-On Covers",
  col   = "steelblue",
  ylim  = c(0, 0.5)
)
```

```{r task2-interpret}
# dental_cover is the most frequent add-on (~35% of policyholders).
# maternity_cover is the rarest (~13%), because it has a lower probability
# for male and older female policyholders in the simulator.
# Rarer items tend to appear in fewer frequent itemsets, so maternity_cover
# will feature in fewer rules unless paired with a very common item.
```

## Task 3: Mine association rules

```{r task3-apriori}
rules <- apriori(
  trans,
  parameter = list(supp = 0.05, conf = 0.70, minlen = 2)
)
summary(rules)
```

```{r task3-top10}
inspect(head(sort(rules, by = "lift"), 10))
```

```{r task3-dental-rules}
dental_rules <- subset(rules, rhs %in% "dental_cover=TRUE")
inspect(sort(dental_rules, by = "lift"))
```

## Task 4: Scatter plot and actionable recommendations

```{r task4-scatter}
plot(
  rules,
  method  = "scatter",
  measure = c("support", "confidence"),
  shading = "lift",
  main    = "Association Rules — Insurance Add-On Covers"
)
```

```{r task4-recommendations}
top3 <- head(sort(rules, by = "lift"), 3)
inspect(top3)

# Rule 1: {vision_cover=TRUE} → {dental_cover=TRUE}  (example, lift ~ 1.8-2.0)
# Recommendation: Target all policyholders who hold vision cover but not dental
# with a bundled dental add-on offer. The high lift means they are ~2x more
# likely than average to accept, justifying a targeted (lower-cost) campaign.

# Rule 2: {mental_cover=TRUE} → {dental_cover=TRUE}  (example)
# Recommendation: When a policyholder contacts the insurer to add mental health
# cover, proactively suggest dental cover at the same time — the co-occurrence
# rate is high enough to make this a natural upsell moment.

# Rule 3: {vision_cover=TRUE, mental_cover=TRUE} → {dental_cover=TRUE}  (example)
# Recommendation: Policyholders holding both vision and mental cover are the
# strongest candidates for a "premium care" bundle including dental. Design a
# three-add-on bundle product priced attractively for this segment.
```
